briefing: A 34-second video is spreading online claiming a vessel collision near a disputed maritime feature. Public pressure is rising. A policy office wants language within 30 minutes. The evidence is messy, incomplete, and potentially sensitive.
debrief_prompts: What evidence did the player treat as stronger than it really was?
Did the player protect civilians before release?
Did the controlled language match the confidence level?
Which evidence markings actually changed your final confidence and release posture?

evidence_cards.description: Low-resolution video. No original metadata. Shows two vessels close together, but angle and timing are unclear.
evidence_cards.title: Viral 34-Second Video

evidence_cards.description: One vessel track is visible. The second vessel has a gap during the alleged impact window.
evidence_cards.title: Incomplete AIS Track

evidence_cards.description: Witness account reports a similar event but gives a different time than the viral post. Identity and location could expose the witness community.
evidence_cards.title: Fisherfolk Witness Report

evidence_cards.description: A translated caption uses the word 'attack,' but the original phrase could also mean 'collision' or 'impact.'
evidence_cards.title: Translation Note

evidence_cards.description: Multiple newly created accounts are repeating casualty claims without a primary source.
evidence_cards.title: Amplification Alert

facilitator_notes: This scenario tests whether players resist viral attribution pressure when media metadata is missing.
The defensible early confidence range is Possible / Unverified / Manipulated or Unclear.
Watch whether the player protects the fisherfolk witness before public release.
Watch whether players flag viral/bot evidence and mark civilian-risk evidence sensitive before finalizing.
learning_objectives: Avoid public attribution when metadata and source integrity are weak
Protect civilian witnesses and communities before release
Use controlled language to slow escalation
Trigger information-integrity review when bot amplification or manipulated media is suspected

release_options.label: Release cautious language: aware of reports; media not authenticated; review ongoing.
Release strong attribution: intentional hostile act confirmed.
Hold all public comment pending further verification.
Issue information-integrity caution: circulating media and casualty claims are unverified.

title: Scenario 01: The Viral Collision Video
